# SECTION IV: OVERALL LANGUAGE CONSIDERATION
findings.why_it_matters: Page 146 (folio III-26) ends with the 77-Level-Description-Entry glossary definition; it prints no Section IV heading. The markdown adds a level-1 '# SECTION IV: OVERALL LANGUAGE CONSIDERATION' after the III-26 folio, while page 147 already carries the printed heading as '## <u>SECTION IV: OVERALL LANGUAGE CONSIDERATION</u>'. The section heading is therefore duplicated, at two different levels, and one copy sits on a page that does not print it.

The printed subsection heading is transcribed as a plain paragraph, while its siblings 2.1.1 and 2.1.2 on page 147 and 2.1.7 on page 149 are '####' headings. The heading is demoted, so the document outline loses 2.1.3.

Plain paragraph rather than a '####' heading like its siblings 2.1.1, 2.1.2 and 2.1.7. This is the notation clause cited by the reconciliation and figure-checking work (IV.2.1.4); a heading-based locator cannot find it.
Plain paragraph rather than a '####' heading like its siblings 2.1.1, 2.1.2 and 2.1.7; the outline loses the Ellipsis clause (IV.2.1.5).
Plain paragraph rather than a '####' heading like its siblings 2.1.1, 2.1.2 and 2.1.7; the outline loses clause IV.2.1.6.

The printed peers '2. NOTATION USED IN FORMATS' / '2.1 DEFINITION OF A GENERAL FORMAT' are transcribed at '###' / '####' on page 147, but '3. RULES' / '3.1' / '3.2' are at '##' / '###'. Clause 3 sits one level higher than its sibling clause 2 (at the same level as the SECTION IV heading), so the outline nests the section wrongly.
The printed subsection heading is a plain paragraph in the markdown (compare '### 3.1 SYNTAX RULES' on page 149 and '### 4.2.2 Character-Strings' on page 151); the outline loses clause IV.4.1.
Plain paragraph rather than a heading; the outline loses clause IV.4.2, the parent of the '### 4.2.2 Character-Strings' heading on page 151.
Plain paragraph rather than a heading, while its sibling 4.2.2 on page 151 is '### 4.2.2 Character-Strings'; the outline loses the Separators clause IV.4.2.1.

Plain paragraph rather than a heading, while its siblings '#### 4.2.2.1.1 User-Defined Words' (page 152) and '#### 4.2.2.1.4 Function-Names' (page 155) are headings; the outline loses clause IV.4.2.2.1.2.
Plain paragraph rather than a heading, while its siblings 4.2.2.1.1 and 4.2.2.1.4 are '####' headings; the outline loses the Reserved Words clause IV.4.2.2.1.3.
Plain paragraph rather than a heading, while its siblings '#### 4.2.2.1.3.2 Optional Words' and '#### 4.2.2.1.3.3 Special Purpose Words' on page 155 are headings.
